newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power dips on rainy weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power dips on rainy weekend.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic dipped Friday on expected flat power demand amid forecasts of cloudy, rainy weather over the weekend, brokers and traders said.
"With the rain and everything, there isn't a lot demand," said one regional trader. "Monday is overcast, rainy."

In the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, electricity prices for firm, peak delivery on Saturday was quoted at $17.50-$19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh); Sunday $17.50-$18.50; and Monday $21.50-$22.50.
PJM firm, peak power on Thursday for Friday delivery was discussed at $22.00-$23.00.
Off-peak, firm PJM power from Saturday to Monday was offered in the $13.50 area, down from Thursday's $15.00.
PJM firm, peak electricity for next week was valued at $22.00-$23.00, a wider range that Thursday's $22.00.
Peak power for firm, peak delivery for the rest of September was talked between $21.75 and $22.00, unchanged from Thursday.
Forward PJM prices today were generally flat from Thursday's levels.
October firm, peak PJM electricity was assessed at $20.50-$20.75; November $21.50-$21.90; and December $25.35-$25.85.
PJM power prices for the fourth quarter was quoted at $22.50-$22.75, compared with Thursday's $22.45-$22.75 range.
